claim: A correction turn ('I meant…', 'scratch that', 'not X, Y', 'that transcription was wrong') SUPERSEDES the prior turn: the bad/misheard content is not durably stored, and the corrected meaning is what Vera carries forward.
owner: anima/repair.py (the deterministic CONVERSATION-REPAIR seam: detect a value correction, resolve the slot from the rejected old value, supersede via Facts.merge correction), anima/server.py (_turn repair seam — short-circuits before the LLM, ships through final_output_gate, backend 'repair:supersede'), anima/memory_lirf.py (Facts.merge: old->history 'user-corrected' / new active @0.97), anima/mouth.py (final_output_gate, response_complete)

killer_test.name: correction_supersedes_and_bad_transcript_not_stored
killer_test.setup: Hermetic temp store. Turn 1 states a wrong fact (e.g. 'my dog's name is Rex'). Turn 2 corrects it ('sorry, scratch that — not Rex, his name is Atlas' / 'that transcription was wrong, I said Atlas'). Assert: after Turn 2, memory_lirf.about(name) / <name>.lirf.json contains the corrected value (Atlas) and does NOT durably retain the superseded one (Rex) as the active fact; a follow-up 'what's my dog's name?' answers Atlas. The MRI capture frame for Turn 2 shows the correction lifted. Real .anima byte-unchanged.

known_gaps: RESOLVED (2026-06-06): the missing supersede-the-last-turn primitive was built as anima/repair.py and wired into server._turn as a deterministic seam (precedence: host -> reference -> repair -> lerf -> normal). On the anchorless killer phrasing 'scratch that — not Rex, his name is Atlas' the seam reads the rejected old value (Rex), finds the active ledger row holding it (dog_name), and folds the new value (Atlas) through Facts.merge(correction=True): Rex -> history[] (reason 'user-corrected', never deleted), Atlas -> active @0.97. The confirmation ships through the SAME #1-rule final_output_gate (backend 'repair:supersede', no LLM, no second return path) and the Whole-System MRI records the seam. Proven by scripts/certify_repair.py (Rex->Atlas->Cooper, 23 checks, CERTIFIED) and probe_conversation_repair (drives the real server._turn + a deterministic model-free follow-up via memory_lirf.retrieve). The seam supersedes only a slot it can PROVE holds the rejected value (or, on the 'his name is X' form, an existing NAME-type row) -> never mis-corrects, never hijacks a normal turn (honest fall-through to the pipeline). Out of scope for this seam: list-trait edits (likes/dislikes) — a remove-one-item op, tracked separately.
